clue.text: When news is on usually officer listens

parts.note: ITV's News at Ten is broadcast at ten o'clock, so the news is usually on AT TEN
DS is a Detective Sergeant, a police officer

explanation.surface: A police officer habitually tunes in when the evening news is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a long-running British evening news programme, so 'when news is on' is AT TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to pay heed or give ear, a close synonym of listening.

clue.text: Demand Yankee auditor's time of reckoning?

parts.note: a tax is a demand for payment
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an auditor is a listener, whose organ is the ear

explanation.surface: An American is asked what the accountant's audit period is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, which fits the tax theme, but here it is someone who hears.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax year is the period over which tax liability is reckoned, hence playful reckoning.

clue.text: Record trouble with canal — it is vanishing

indicators.note: vanishing means the letters of it is disappear from the condition

parts.note: enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, the alimentary canal

explanation.surface: Someone logs a problem on a waterway that is disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway, but it is the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, as in a ledger or log.

clue.text: Stripped duke finished hiding uniform

indicators.note: hiding means the completed word conceals the letter within

parts.note: ended means finished
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A naked duke has finished concealing his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded means laid bare, so stripped of covering.

clue.text: Check scenery support

parts.note: a stage set is the scenery
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the frame that holds up stage scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like an instruction to inspect, but it is the noun: a reverse or hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a halt to progress, and a setback is exactly such a reverse.

clue.text: Abstain from drug that is cut

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
sc., short for scilicet, means namely or that is
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give up a narcotic that has been adulterated.
explanation.walkthrough: sc. (scilicet) is a Latin abbreviation meaning 'that is to say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to deliberately avoid or shun, the same as refraining from.

clue.text: Bachelor eats with son running round? Such vulgarity!

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: running round means the two letters surround the eating word

parts.note: to dine is to eat, so eats is dines

explanation.surface: A single man dines while his son races round the table, to general disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running round' is not the son's behaviour: it tells 'with son' (W and S) to go around 'eats'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawdiness is coarse, lewd humour, a kind of crude vulgarity.

clue.text: Almost cut short new hanging

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to curtail is to cut short

explanation.surface: Someone nearly trimmed a fresh drape too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' sounds like an execution, but it is a noun for drapery.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a length of cloth hung at a window or stage, a hanging.

clue.text: Engineer examined such a dramatic device

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A technician has inspected a theatrical contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally 'god from the machine', the crane that lowered a god onto the Greek stage to resolve the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a plot contrivance that resolves a drama abruptly, originally theatrical stage machinery.

clue.text: Leave Egypt's borders around eleven

indicators.note: around tells us the outer letters wrap about the Roman number
the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A traveller departs from the frontier regions of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave and to exit are synonyms for going out of a place.

clue.text: Xmas missive inspiring old western playwright

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

indicators.note: inspiring is read as breathing in, so the card takes letters inside it

parts.note: a card is a short written message

explanation.surface: A Christmas card brings to mind an old cowboy film for a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was the English playwright of Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward was a celebrated English dramatist and wit of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Juliet swung round topless, getting derided

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is lost from the top of the word

parts.note: to swing round is to veer, so swung round is veered

explanation.surface: A topless Juliet spins round and is mocked by the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeering is mocking someone loudly, so to be jeered is to be derided.

clue.text: Woman smuggled documents inside for playwright

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: inside places the documents within the smuggling word

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran
ID is identity documents

explanation.surface: A woman smuggled papers in her luggage on behalf of a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan was an Irish-born dramatist of eighteenth-century comedies of manners.

clue.text: Fancy Dorothy scoffing beef as standard practice!

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the rearranged name takes in the beast
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: Elaborate Dorothy gobbling roast beef is held up as the normal way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is not meat here but the animal it comes from; 'Fancy' gives ORTHODY, which swallows the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodoxy is conformity with accepted, established norms, the usual or approved way of doing things.

clue.text: One in the pits wears this halo?

definitions.text: One in the pits wears this halo?

parts.words: One in the pits wears this halo?
parts.note: a miner in a coal pit wears a lamp on his helmet, which is a light round the head like a halo

explanation.walkthrough: 'Halo' is read literally as a light on the head, the kind a coal miner straps to his helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp worn on the forehead by a miner gives light, rather like a saint's glowing ring.

clue.text: Stainer's notes held by male alto

definitions.note: read as 'stainer is': henna is a dye that stains hair and skin

indicators.note: held by means the notes sit inside the other letters

parts.note: he refers to a male
A is the abbreviation for alto in music
N is note, so two notes give NN

explanation.surface: Notes by the composer John Stainer, sung by a male alto.
explanation.walkthrough: Stainer looks like the Victorian composer, fitting the notes and alto, but it is something that stains.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used to colour hair and decorate skin.

clue.text: Book range in the end but not completely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book of maps
second meaning: the Atlas Mountains of north-west Africa

indicators.note: not completely means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: at last means finally, in the end

explanation.surface: A book about a mountain range that is never quite finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, and the Atlas is a mountain range in Morocco.

clue.text: The Stage article about enthralling atmosphere

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the outer letters hold the unit

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about, concerning
at is an abbreviation for a technical atmosphere, a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: An article in The Stage, the theatre trade paper, about a gripping atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stage is the British theatre newspaper, but here it means the dramatic world.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre, as an art and profession, is what people mean by the stage.

clue.text: Computer's the way to capture Joe's tricky display

indicators.note: to capture means the computer letters close around the soldier

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer; with the 's that gives MACS
GI Joe is an American soldier, so Joe gives GI
how means the way something is done

explanation.surface: A computer is the means to record Joe's display of tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic show is a performance of conjuring tricks, a display of illusion.

clue.text: Individual is firm about dramatist

indicators.note: about means the two letters go round the individual

parts.note: one is a single individual
Co is a company, a firm

explanation.surface: A single person is stubborn about a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Ionesco was the Romanian-French writer of absurdist plays such as Rhinoceros.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionesco was a leading playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Note Norma perhaps fronting work in 18

indicators.note: fronting means the opera comes ahead of the note

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini, an example of one
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A note about Bellini's Norma heading a production in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is THEATRE, here the operating theatre where surgeons work.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate in an operating theatre, the place where they do their work.

clue.text: Hose this GT after it's overhauled

indicators.note: an overhauled car is taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Wash this GT sports car with a hose once it has been serviced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a verb for washing a car, but it is the noun for stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is a term for legwear, such as stockings and tights.

clue.text: After spring, darkness reduced, just about

indicators.note: after places the darkness word behind the spring

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: night is darkness

explanation.surface: Following spring, the dark nights are shorter, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh means almost or nearly, so very close to completely.

clue.text: Tidy jasmine at entrance, clipping what's choking it

indicators.note: clipping off the outer growth leaves the letters inside the phrase, the part choked by it

explanation.surface: A gardener trims the weeds smothering jasmine by the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to make orderly, a synonym for the verb to tidy.

clue.text: Behave badly in a time-consuming contest

indicators.note: consuming means the contest swallows up the letter

parts.note: a cup is a competition, such as the FA Cup

explanation.surface: A player misbehaves in a long, drawn-out match.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, as of children or malfunctioning machines.

clue.text: Cast hated snags, the ones behind the scenes

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould anew, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The actors loathed hitches, unlike the crew working backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagehands work backstage moving scenery and props, literally behind the scenes.

clue.text: Squad leaves at start of Macbeth

parts.note: tea is a drink made from leaves

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the play's title

explanation.surface: A troupe walks out right as Macbeth begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a group working or playing together, such as a team.

clue.text: One examines canines first after depression

indicators.note: after puts the ordinal behind the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow depression
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A vet looks over the dogs first after an attack of the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs and a vet, but it means the pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine teeth are checked by a dental surgeon, who examines teeth.

clue.text: Stuck in woods, Romeo can't help giggling

indicators.note: stuck in means the letter is lodged inside the woods

parts.note: copses are small woods
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo, lost in a forest, cannot stop laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: In actors' slang to corpse is to break into uncontrollable laughter on stage, fitting the theatrical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang: an actor who corpses ruins a scene by laughing helplessly.
